digest.component_or_area: Gerrit Verified CI pipeline / Ubuntu runner scheduling
propositions: Ubuntu default-tier test jobs occupy 30+ runner-minutes per Verified run while macOS is completion critical path, due to redundant YAML I/O in bridge cadence test, repeated Pandoc subprocess calls in render tests, and fixture setup overhead.

Bridge cadence test loads and parses workflow YAML 1,440 times inside a comprehension (0.38ms per parse * 1,440 iterations) rather than once, consuming 6+ runner-minutes; hoisting the parse preserves the exhaustive minute checks without changing test assertions.

Pandoc render suite executes 3,421+ Pandoc subprocesses for full corpus and hardening tests; static golden fixtures paired with small real Pandoc boundary contracts preserve ADR 0095 assertions while moving full corpus replay to scheduled External Integration workflow.

Editor loopback fixture setup (35s on macOS, 49s on Ubuntu py3.13) is dominated by socket.getfqdn calls; attributed mechanism differs from test assertions and remediation requires nested timing instrumentation.

Gerrit Verified jobs with always() predicates in if conditions persist across superseded patchsets because GitHub does not send cancellation when the condition remains true; merged cancellation repair (Gerrit 1792) uses !cancelled() status check to stop stale runs.

Post-remediation full-route Gerrit Verified runs achieved 20-30 minute completion target (mean 24m58s, N=3) after landing schedule I/O hoist, static Pandoc corpus with external full-replay oracle, AST provenance index, editor fixture instrumentation, build-provenance package optimization, and repo_policy singleton routing without removing behavioral coverage or adding parallel workers.
